1. Local Extrema and Critical Points

1 lecture · 8 textbook (total 9)

Local minimumf has a local minimum at p if f(p) is less than or equal to the values of f for points near p.
Local maximumf has a local maximum at p if f(p) is greater than or equal to the values of f for points near p.
Critical pointA point p in the domain of f where f′(p)=0 or f′(p) is undefined. The point (p,f(p)) on the graph is also called a critical point. The critical value is f(p).
Where to lookIf a continuous function has a local max or min at p, then p is a critical point or an endpoint of the interval. A function may have any number of critical points or none. Warning: not every critical point is a local max or min.
1
Lecture Question · Ex 1
Find all critical points of f(x)=x3−9x2−48x+52.
Answerx=−2, x=8
Full solutionDf​=R (polynomial)
f′(x)=3x2−18x−48
f′(x)=0: 3x2−18x−48=0⇒3(x2−6x−16)=0
⇒x2−6x−16=0⇒(x+2)(x−8)=0
x=−2∈D,   x=8∈D
(or use the quadratic formula with a=3, b=−18, c=−48:
x=618±324+576​​=618±30​, so x=8 or x=−2)
f′(x) DNE: no solution (polynomial).
Critical points: x=−2, x=8​
Note: the typed notes show +9x2; the doctor corrected it to −9x2, which is the function used in Examples 2 and 4.

Textbook Question · Problem 5
  • (a) Graph a function with two local minima and one local maximum.
  • (b) Graph a function with two critical points. One of these critical points should be a local minimum, and the other should be neither a local maximum nor a local minimum.
Answer(a) W shape, e.g. x4−2x2   (b) e.g. x4+4x3
Full solution(a) A “W” shape: down to a valley (local min), up to a hilltop (local max), down to a second valley (local min), then up. Example: f(x)=x4−2x2 (min at x=±1, max at x=0).
Answer 5(a)
(b) Down to a valley (local min), then up, flatten out for a moment with a horizontal tangent (critical point, neither), then keep going up. Example: f(x)=x4+4x3, f′(x)=4x2(x+3): x=−3 local min, x=0 neither.
Answer 5(b)

Textbook Question · Problem 6
During an illness a person ran a fever. His temperature rose steadily for eighteen hours, then went steadily down for twenty hours. When was there a critical point for his temperature as a function of time?
AnswerAt t=18 hours
Full solutionAt t=18​ hours. The temperature changes from increasing to decreasing there, so it is a critical point (a local maximum).

Textbook Question · Problem 7
Graph two continuous functions f and g, each of which has exactly five critical points, the points A–E in Figure 4.12, and which satisfy the following conditions:
Figure 4.12
  • (a) f(x)→∞ as x→−∞   and   f(x)→∞ as x→∞
  • (b) g(x)→−∞ as x→−∞   and   g(x)→0 as x→∞
Answer(a) A,B neither, C min, D max, E min   (b) A max, B neither, C min, D max, E min
Full solution(a) Coming down from +∞, f flattens at A and at B (horizontal tangent, neither) while still decreasing, falls to a local min at C, rises to a local max at D, falls to a local min at E, then rises to +∞.
Answer 7(a)
(b) Coming up from −∞, g rises to a local max at A, decreases and flattens at B (neither), falls to a local min at C, rises to a local max at D, falls to a local min at E, then rises toward 0 (approaching the x-axis from below).
Answer 7(b)

If U and V are positive constants, find all critical points of F(t)=Uet+Ve−t.
Answert=0.5ln(V/U)
Full solutionF′(t)=Uet−Ve−t=0⇒Uet=Ve−t⇒e2t=UV​⇒2t=lnUV​

2. The First Derivative Test

3 lecture · 9 textbook (total 12)

First derivative testIf f changes from decreasing to increasing at p (f′: − to +), f has a local minimum at p. If f changes from increasing to decreasing at p (f′: + to −), f has a local maximum at p.
Steps1. Domain   2. Find f′   3. Solve f′(x)=0 and f′(x) DNE (keep only points in the domain)   4. Sign table with test numbers   5. Conclusion   6. Value f(p)
10
Lecture Question · Ex 2
Let f(x)=x3−9x2−48x+52. Use the first derivative test to confirm that f has a local maximum at x=−2 and a local minimum at x=8.
AnswerLocal max f(−2)=104; local min f(8)=−396
Full solutionFrom Example 1: f′(x)=3x2−18x−48, critical points x=−2 and x=8.
Test numbers: −3, 0, 9:   f′(−3)=33>0,   f′(0)=−48<0,   f′(9)=33>0
x−∞ to −2−2 to 88 to ∞
f′(x)+−+
f(x)↗↘↗
f is increasing before −2 and decreasing after −2, so f has a local max at x=−2:
f(−2)=(−2)3−9(−2)2−48(−2)+52=104​
f is decreasing before 8 and increasing after 8, so f has a local min at x=8:
f(8)=(8)3−9(8)2−48(8)+52=−396​

Textbook Question · Problem 37
  • (a) On a computer or calculator, graph f(θ)=θ−sinθ. Can you tell whether the function has any zeros in the interval 0≤θ≤1?
  • (b) Find f′. What does the sign of f′ tell you about the zeros of f in the interval 0≤θ≤1?
Answer(a) θ=0; can't tell other zeros   (b) f′=1−cosθ>0: only zero at θ=0
Full solution(a) f(0)=0, so θ=0 is a zero. Near 0 the graph is so flat (very close to the axis) that you cannot tell from the graph whether there are other zeros in 0≤θ≤1.
(b) f′(θ)=1−cosθ>0 for 0<θ≤1. So f is increasing on this interval: starting at f(0)=0 it only goes up. The only zero is at the origin, θ=0.

3. The Second Derivative Test

1 lecture · 3 textbook (total 4)

Second derivative testIf f′(p)=0 and f′′(p)>0 (concave up), f has a local minimum at p. If f′(p)=0 and f′′(p)<0 (concave down), f has a local maximum at p.
22
Lecture Question · Ex 4
Let f(x)=x3−9x2−48x+52. Use the second derivative test to confirm that f has a local maximum at x=−2 and a local minimum at x=8.
Answerf′′(−2)=−30<0: local max; f′′(8)=30>0: local min
Full solutionFrom Example 1: f′(x)=3x2−18x−48, critical points x=−2 and x=8.
f′′(x)=6x−18
x=−2: f′′(−2)=6(−2)−18=−30<0, so by the 2nd derivative test f has a local max at x=−2.
x=8: f′′(8)=6(8)−18=30>0, so by the 2nd derivative test f has a local min at x=8.
23
Textbook Question · Problem 22
The function f(x)=x4−4x3+8x has a critical point at x=1. Use the second derivative test to identify it as a local maximum or local minimum.
AnswerLocal maximum
Full solutionDomain: all real numbers (−∞,∞).
f′(x)=4x3−12x2+8,   f′(1)=4−12+8=0 (critical point).
f′′(x)=12x2−24x,   f′′(1)=12−24=−12<0 (concave down).
By the 2nd derivative test, x=1 is a local maximum (f(1)=5).

  • (b) Use the second derivative test to determine whether the function has a local maximum or local minimum at each critical point.
Answer(a) x=b   (b) local min
Full solution(a) f′(x)=1−xb​=0⇒x=b​ (the only critical point; f′ is defined for x>0).
(b) f′′(x)=x2b​,   f′′(b)=b1​>0, so f has a local minimum at x=b.

Textbook Question · Problem 33
  • (a) For a a positive constant, find all critical points of f(x)=x−ax​.
  • (b) What value of a gives a critical point at x=5? Does f(x) have a local maximum or a local minimum at this critical point?
Answer(a) x=0, x=4a2​   (b) a=20​; local min
Full solution(a) Domain x≥0. f′(x)=1−2x​a​.
f′(x)=0⇒x​=2a​⇒x=4a2​;   f′(x) DNE at x=0 (in the domain). Critical points: x=0, x=4a2​​
(b) 4a2​=5⇒a2=20⇒a=20​=25​≈4.47​
f′′(x)=4a​x−3/2>0 at x=5, so it is a local minimum.

Graph a function f with the following properties:
• f(x) has critical points at x=2 and x=5;

Textbook Question · Problem 36
Assume f has a derivative everywhere and has just one critical point, at x=3. In parts (a)–(d), you are given additional conditions. In each case decide whether x=3 is a local maximum, a local minimum, or neither. Explain your reasoning. Sketch possible graphs for all four cases.
  • (a) f′(1)=3 and f′(5)=−1
  • (b) f(x)→∞ as x→∞ and as x→−∞
  • (c) f(1)=1, f(2)=2, f(4)=4, f(5)=5
  • (d) f′(2)=−1, f(3)=1, f(x)→3 as x→∞
Answer(a) max   (b) min   (c) neither   (d) min
Full solutionSince x=3 is the only critical point, f′ cannot change sign except at x=3: f is increasing or decreasing on all of x<3, and on all of x>3.
(a) f′(1)>0: increasing left of 3; f′(5)<0: decreasing right of 3. Local maximum. Sketch: a single hill with its top at x=3.
(b) f must come down from ∞ and go back up to ∞: decreasing then increasing. Local minimum. Sketch: a single valley (U shape) with its bottom at x=3.
(c) f(1)<f(2): increasing left of 3; f(4)<f(5): increasing right of 3. Neither. Sketch: always rising, with a flat spot (horizontal tangent) at x=3.
(d) f′(2)<0: decreasing left of 3. Right of 3, f goes from f(3)=1 toward 3, so it increases. Local minimum. Sketch: falling to a low point (3,1), then rising and leveling off toward the line y=3.

5. Families of Functions and Parameters

1 lecture · 10 textbook (total 11)

Critical pointA point p in the domain of f where f′(p)=0 or f′(p) is undefined. The point (p,f(p)) on the graph is also called a critical point. The critical value is f(p).
Second derivative testIf f′(p)=0 and f′′(p)>0 (concave up), f has a local minimum at p. If f′(p)=0 and f′′(p)<0 (concave down), f has a local maximum at p.

Find the critical point of the function f(x)=x2+bx+c. What is its graphical significance?
Answerx=−2b​ (local min): the vertex of the parabola
Full solutionDf​=R (polynomial)
f′(x)=2x+b
f′(x)=0⇒2x+b=0⇒2x=−b⇒x=−2b​​∈D
f′′(x)=2,   f′′(−2b​)=2>0, so by the 2nd derivative test f has a local min at x=−2b​.
Graphical significance: the critical point x=−2b​ is the vertex of the parabola, the graph of the quadratic function.

Textbook Question · Problem 24
Investigate the one-parameter family of functions. Assume that a is positive.
f(x)=(x−a)2
  • (a) Graph f(x) using three different values for a.
  • (b) Using your graph in part (a), describe the critical points of f and how they appear to move as a increases.
  • (c) Find a formula for the x-coordinates of the critical point(s) of f in terms of a.
Answerx=a (local min), moves right
Full solution(a) For a=1,2,3: three identical upward parabolas with vertices at (1,0), (2,0), (3,0).
(b) Each graph has one critical point, a local minimum at the vertex on the x-axis. As a increases, it moves to the right.
(c) f′(x)=2(x−a)=0⇒x=a​

Textbook Question · Problem 25
Investigate the one-parameter family of functions. Assume that a is positive.
f(x)=x3−ax
  • (a) Graph f(x) using three different values for a.
  • (b) Using your graph in part (a), describe the critical points of f and how they appear to move as a increases.
  • (c) Find a formula for the x-coordinates of the critical point(s) of f in terms of a.
Answerx=±a/3​, move farther from origin
Full solution(a) For example a=1,2,3: cubics through the origin, each with a hump (local max) to the left of the origin and a dip (local min) to the right; larger a gives a bigger hump and dip.
Answer 25(a)
(b) Two critical points: a local max at negative x and a local min at positive x. As a increases they move farther from the origin.
(c) f′(x)=3x2−a=0⇒x=±a/3​​   (−a/3​: local max, +a/3​: local min)

Textbook Question · Problem 26
Investigate the one-parameter family of functions. Assume that a is positive.
f(x)=x2e−ax
  • (a) Graph f(x) using three different values for a.
  • (b) Using your graph in part (a), describe the critical points of f and how they appear to move as a increases.
  • (c) Find a formula for the x-coordinates of the critical point(s) of f in terms of a.
Answerx=0 and x=a2​
Full solution(a) For a=1,2,3: each graph touches the origin (minimum), rises to a hump, then decays toward 0 as x→∞ (and grows to ∞ as x→−∞). Larger a gives a lower hump closer to the origin.
(b) Two critical points: a local min at x=0 (does not move) and a local max at x>0, which moves toward the origin (and gets lower: f(2/a)=a2e24​) as a increases.
(c) f′(x)=2xe−ax−ax2e−ax=xe−ax(2−ax)=0⇒x=0, x=a2​​

Textbook Question · Problem 29
Sketch several members of the family y=x3−ax2 on the same axes. Discuss the effect of the parameter a on the graph. Find all critical points for this function.
Answerx=0, x=32a​
Full solutiony′=3x2−2ax=x(3x−2a)=0⇒x=0, x=32a​​
For a>0: local max at x=0 (value 0), local min at x=32a​ (value −274a3​). For a<0 the roles swap (max at 32a​, min at 0). For a=0, y=x3 has one critical point, x=0, which is neither.
Effect of a: every graph passes through the origin; as a (positive) increases, the dip moves right and gets deeper. The local minima lie on the curve y=−21​x3.
